text: Sunny found a creek beneath the silver moon,
its water still and smooth as polished glass.
A ring appeared, and then another ring —
something moving softly through the stream.
A platypus, with fur like velvet brown,
a duck-like bill and webbed and paddling feet.
It glided slow across the silver creek,
leaving gentle ripples in its wake.
“Hello,” said Sunny. “What a lovely swim.”
“The water's warm and quiet now,” it said.
It dived beneath with barely any splash,
and came back up with whiskers dripping bright.
It floated on its back to watch the stars,
paws upon its round and fluffy tummy.
“At night the creek is calm,” the platypus said.
“The perfect place to drift and softly dream.”
They watched the moon float on the water's face,
two moons now — one above and one below.
The platypus gave one last happy paddle,
then slipped into its burrow by the bank.
Sunny found a nest of reeds nearby
and curled up warm beside the whispering creek.
The water murmured soft its lullaby.
Everything was gentle, calm, and safe.
Her eyes grew heavy as the ripples slowed.
One slow blink… then another… then no more.
And Sunny slept beside the sleeping stream,
rocked by dreams as soft as flowing water.
Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, little platypus.
Goodnight, sleepy creek. Goodnight, little one.
